1.why: All ten screens show a static, uncluttered layout with no moving images, animations, or pop-ups.

2.why: Blue primary buttons, highlighted Next-step banners, and the active progress pill clearly stand out on every page.

3.why: Persistent stepper, page title, Next-step banner, and labeled fields make the required action easy to locate quickly.

4.why: The always-visible 8-step stepper plus per-page Next-step text mean the user need not memorize rules or sequence.

5.why: No remember-me checkbox, password-manager affordance, or autofill control appears on sign-in or password screens.

6.why: Sign-in prefills the familiar email helena@hospital.test and the stepper marks completed stages the user already passed.

7.why: Labels and body copy are short, plain sentences (e.g., Next-step lines, brief policy text) that are easy to read.

8.why: No error states are shown in any screenshot, so there is no evidence error messages describe problems or fixes.

9.why: Simulated delivery and MFA codes are displayed as concrete values to enter; password page gives rules but no example password.

10.why: Password and one-time-code fields are clearly labeled at their steps, yet no alternative methods such as face login are offered.

11.why: Each screen presents one primary button and at most a single secondary link, avoiding choice overload.

12.why: Explicit success copy appears after key actions (Password saved; Appointment request confirmed) stating the outcome.

13.why: Every page includes a Next-step tip banner, safety reminder, and a collapsible Help and safe authentication section.

14.why: Links such as Use a different email address, Return to sign in, and Reset password instead let the user back up and retry.

15.why: Header, stepper, card layout, Next-step pattern, button style, help block, and footer remain identical across all steps.
